### Suspicion
Author: One Year Devotions for Men
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/suspicion-one-year-devotions-for-men-october-2.html
Passage: Numbers 5:29-30
Points:
- Unlike modern private views of morality, Israel viewed marital faithfulness as vital to the stability of the whole community.
- The prescribed ritual took matters out of the husband's hands and placed them before God and the priest.
- Compared to neighboring ancient cultures where accused wives were thrown into rivers, Israel's law provided protection and divine arbitration.
- Marital suspicion today must be resolved through honest, transparent communication and mutual prayer before the Lord.

### Fidelity Check
Author: Marian V. Liautaud
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/niv-devotions-for-couples/niv-devotions-for-couples-week-of-apr-11.html
Passage: Numbers 5:15
Points:
- Jealousy and suspicion can easily arise and threaten the stability of a marriage.
- A foundational defense against infidelity is acknowledging vulnerability and praying for God's protection.
- Couples cultivate safety by practicing open communication and establishing voluntary accountability checkpoints.
- Embracing transparency rather than defensiveness relieves anxiety and actively rebuilds fractured trust.

### Is Numbers 5 Unjust to Women?
Author: Wendy Alsup
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/numbers-5-women/
Passage: Numbers 5:11-31
Points:
- Rather than harming women, the law prevented husbands in the ancient world from unilaterally divorcing or executing accused wives.
- Unlike pagan trials by ordeal that required a miracle to survive, an innocent wife was naturally protected by ordinary water and dust.
- The mediating priest foreshadowed Jesus Christ, who intercedes for His people and silences accusations.
- On the cross, Jesus took the curse upon Himself so that the guilty could find pardon.

### The Case Study of the Jealous Husband of Numbers 5
Author: Angie Velasquez Thornton
Site: The Gospel Coalition Canada
URL: https://ca.thegospelcoalition.org/columns/femmes-scriptura/how-to-interpret-difficult-passages-of-scripture-the-case-study-of-the-jealous-husband-of-numbers-5/
Passage: Numbers 5:11-31
Points:
- Close examination of difficult Old Testament statutes reveals unexpected divine mercy and care toward women.
- The ritual provided institutional access and safety for a wife against a husband's unchecked jealousy.
- An innocent woman was publicly vindicated before the congregation because harmless dust in water required direct divine judgment to punish.
- The broader gospel message assures that those guilty of secret sins can receive complete forgiveness at the cross.
